question: The OIDAC Europe 2025 report recorded 2 211 incidents of anti-Christian hate crimes in Europe in 2024, including 274 attacks against individuals. In Greece, the General Secretariat for Religious Affairs recorded 399 incidents against Orthodox places of worship in 2024 and 362 in 2025, including theft, vandalism and desecration.

Examples include the desecration of Agios Achilleios in Larissa (2024), the destruction of religious icons at the Church of Agia Olga in Athens (2025), the beating of a priest in Nea Ionia in Volos (2025) and the desecration of a small shrine in Saronikos (2026). The motives for these incidents need to be investigated.

At the same time, while there are European Coordinators for combating antisemitism and anti-Muslim hatred, no such figure exists for anti-Christian hatred, despite a related request being made by the European Parliament in its resolution of 21 January 2026. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it intend to appoint a Coordinator for combatting anti-Christian hatred, responding to the European Parliament’s request and ensuring equal institutional protection for all religious communities?
How does it assess the implementation of Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA and Directive 2012/29/EU as regards the protection of Christians against hate crime?
Will it establish a harmonised inventory of anti-Christian attacks, keeping a clear record of church desecrations, attacks against clergy and proven religious motives?
